Seminar Title:

A Multidimensional Evaluation of INSAT-3D HEM and IMC Hourly Rainfall Estimates Using Ground-Based Observations over Southern India

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Name:

Ramvath Ashokkumar ( Rollno : 923er5006)

Nagaraju Chilukoti

Abstract:

Accurate representation of the diurnal cycle of rainfall is essential for understanding monsoon dynamics and improving satellite-based precipitation retrievals. Although INSAT-3D HEM and IMC products are widely used for near-real-time rainfall monitoring, their ability to reproduce the hourly evolution and diurnal cycle of monsoon rainfall remains largely unexplored. This study evaluates the performance of INSAT-3D Hydro-Estimator Method (HEM) and INSAT Multispectral Rainfall-Corrected (IMC) hourly precipitation estimates during the Southwest Monsoon (June&ndashSeptember) over Telangana and Andhra Pradesh for the period 2020&ndash2024 using hourly Self-Recording Rain Gauge (SRRG) observations as reference dataset. The products were assessed through diurnal rainfall analyses at regional, coastal&ndashinland, and sub-regional scales, together with statistical verification. Both products reproduced the broad temporal evolution of the diurnal rainfall cycle but systematically overestimated rainfall magnitude and variability. IMC consistently outperformed HEM by reducing the seasonal RMSE from 6.21 to 5.29 mm h⁻&sup1, mean absolute error from 1.04 to 0.99 mm h⁻&sup1, and standard deviation from 6.18 to 5.25 mm h⁻&sup1, indicating improved representation of rainfall magnitude and variability. However, both products exhibited similarly weak temporal agreement with observations (correlation coefficient &asymp 0.15), suggesting that improvements primarily relate to error reduction rather than the representation of hourly rainfall timing. Taylor diagram and diurnal analyses further confirmed that IMC more closely reproduced the observed rainfall evolution than HEM, particularly during the mature monsoon phase. The findings provide a comprehensive hourly-scale assessment of INSAT-3D precipitation products and offer valuable guidance for improving operational geostationary satellite rainfall retrievals over the Indian monsoon region.&nbsp
